query: Which embedded hardware targets and micro-benchmarks (CPU, memory, solver) are necessary to justify solver-latency targets and to specify formal fallback controller worst-case stopping distances?

response.query: Which embedded hardware targets and micro-benchmarks (CPU, memory, solver) are necessary to justify solver-latency targets and to specify formal fallback controller worst-case stopping distances?
response.answer: To justify solver-latency targets and specify worst-case stopping distances, embedded hardware targets include microcontrollers like ARM Cortex-M series and FPGAs, with micro-benchmarks focusing on CPU cycles and memory access times.
